notes: Major code MA27. Thirteen upper-division four-unit courses (fifty-two units) total, including the required courses. Up to three upper-division courses may be taken outside the department in an approved applied area by petition. MAE 107, ECON 120A-B-C and MATH 195–199 cannot be counted.

buckets.label: Calculus and linear algebra sequence
buckets.note: One of two sequences: MATH 18 and 20A-B-C-D-E, or Honors Calculus MATH 31AH-BH-CH with MATH 20D (31AH-BH-CH cover MATH 18, 20C and 20E). The count shown is the standard six-course sequence; on the honors path four courses complete it.

buckets.label: Mathematical Reasoning
buckets.note: MATH 109. Students completing MATH 31AH-BH-CH may substitute a four-unit upper-division mathematics elective.

buckets.label: Probability or Statistical Methods
buckets.note: MATH 180A or MATH 183. Duplication of credit exists between MATH 180A/183 and ECON 120A.

buckets.label: Two applied sequences (four courses)
buckets.note: TWO complete sequences from: Combinatorics (MATH 154 or 158, and MATH 184 or 188); Differential Equations (MATH 110 and 130); Numerical Methods (two of MATH 170B-C, 175, 179); Optimization (MATH 171A-B); Probability (MATH 180B-C); Statistics (MATH 181A-B, or any two of MATH 181D, 181F, 185, 189). The audit counts four courses from the combined pool — check that yours form two whole sequences.

buckets.label: Additional upper-division mathematics electives
buckets.note: Chosen from any mathematics course numbered 100–194. The count here is what remains AFTER the required upper-division courses above, which also count toward the total. MATH 195–199 may not be used toward any mathematics major.
